chip-blocks.title: Inside the PF1550
chip-blocks.alt: Block diagram of the PF1550: its function blocks, how they connect and which package pins reach each block.
chip-blocks.description: The PF1550's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches.

chip-capabilities.title: What the PF1550 does
chip-capabilities.alt: Capability map of the PF1550: Battery charger (supported): Charges one Li-ion cell: charge voltage and current, termination, timers, watchdog and the status LED; Power path (supported): Runs the system from the input while the cell charges: input current limit, VSYS minimum, battery FET; Battery thermistor and JEITA (supported): Reads the cell's thermistor and lowers or stops the charge when the cell is too cold or too hot; Buck regulators (supported): Sets SW1 to SW3 per state (run, standby, sleep), with dynamic voltage scaling on SW1 and SW2; LDOs, VREFDDR and VSNVS (supported): Sets LDO1 to LDO3, the DDR reference, the RTC supply, the coin cell charger and the USB PHY regulator; Interrupts and status (supported): Pulls INTB low on a fault or event; the driver reads, latches and clears each interrupt group; Power states and sequencer (guarded): Run, standby, sleep, core off and ship states, with the order rails start and stop in; OTP start-up configuration (not covered): Fuses hold the start-up sequence, voltages and charger defaults; the driver reads the option, never fuses.
chip-capabilities.description: Each card is one function of the PF1550: an icon, its name and what it does for the application. The filled pill says how this driver covers it (legend below); the outlined pills are the chip registers behind it. The coverage table in the README gives the driver calls and the datasheet section of each card.

chip-circuit-typical.title: PF1550: Control connections to a host processor
chip-circuit-typical.alt: Schematic of the PF1550 control connections to a host processor: the chip with U2 Host, R1 resistor 2.2 kΩ, R2 resistor 2.2 kΩ, R3 resistor 10 kΩ; the MCU wires carry the port hooks GpioGet(CtrlPin::Intb), GpioSet(CtrlPin::Standby), Write(), WriteRead().
chip-circuit-typical.description: A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected.

chip-hero.title: PF1550
chip-hero.alt: Overview of the PF1550, a power management IC for battery-powered boards built around a low-power application processor: it charges a single Li-ion cell and supplies the processor, the memory and the peripherals from three buck converters, three linear regulators and an RTC supply. A MCU talks to it over I2C; it drives Supply rails, then Processor and memory; it reads back Charger input, Li-ion cell, Push buttons. Headline figures: 4.1 to 6.0 V charger input on VBUSIN, USB or adapter; 3 x 1.0 A buck converters, two with voltage scaling; 3 LDOs 300 mA, 400 mA and 300 mA; up to 1 A charge current from 100 mA, charge voltage 3.5 to 4.44 V; 400 kHz I2C, fast mode, 7-bit address; 5 x 5 mm 40-pin QFN with exposed pad.
chip-hero.description: The PF1550 in the middle, drawn as its HVQFN-40 package. On the left the MCU that runs the driver, joined to it by I2C. To the right, what the chip drives, in the order the power flows. Below it, what the chip reads back. The tiles at the bottom are the headline numbers, each with the datasheet section and page it comes from.

chip-outline.title: PF1550 package, HVQFN-40
chip-outline.alt: Outline of the PF1550 in HVQFN-40 drawn to scale from above: body 5.0 x 5.0 mm, 40 pins and an exposed pad.
chip-outline.description: The PF1550 package seen from the top and, when the height is known, from the side, drawn to scale: 5.0 x 5.0 mm. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side, evenly spaced; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board.

chip-pinout.title: PF1550 pinout, HVQFN-40
chip-pinout.alt: Pinout of the PF1550 in HVQFN-40, top view: 40 pins and an exposed pad, each with its name, its electrical type as a colour and the driver hook that uses it.
chip-pinout.description: The PF1550 seen from the top, in its HVQFN-40 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad.

chip-wiring-typical.title: Wiring: Control connections to a host processor
chip-wiring-typical.alt: Wiring of the PF1550 for the Control connections to a host processor: Host I2C SDA to SDA (Write(), WriteRead()); Host I2C SCL to SCL (Write(), WriteRead()); Host GPIO (STANDBY) to STANDBY (GpioSet(CtrlPin::Standby)); Host GPIO (INTB) to INTB (GpioGet(CtrlPin::Intb)). Supplies, grounds and the support parts are listed under the drawing.
chip-wiring-typical.description: The Host on the left, the PF1550 in the middle. Each wire is coloured by the chip pin's electrical type and carries the net name and the chip pin number above it and, under it, the driver hook that uses it (and any part on the net). The boxes underneath list the supplies, the support parts and the pins this circuit leaves unconnected.

driver-layers.title: The layers, one of them yours
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: your application calls the PF1550 core, which sends register reads and writes through the I2C port contract to the port class you write, which drives the chip; the core and the contract are the same on every MCU.
driver-layers.description: Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.

i2c-register-read.title: One register read on the I2C bus
i2c-register-read.alt: A register read on the PF1550 I2C bus: the host writes the register address 0x00, repeats the start with the read address, reads one byte and ends with NACK and STOP.
i2c-register-read.description: Participants, left to right: Host and PF1550. The steps run from top to bottom. Host sends START, 0x08 + W, 0x00 (DEVICE_ID) to PF1550. Host sends repeated START, 0x08 + R to PF1550. PF1550 returns 0x7C to Host. Host sends NACK, STOP to PF1550.

one-call-through-the-layers.title: One call through the layers
one-call-through-the-layers.alt: One call through the layers: your code calls SetRailVoltage(Ldo1, 2.8 V), the core exchanges frames with the chip through your port and returns the result to your code.
one-call-through-the-layers.description: Participants, left to right: Your code, PF1550<Port> and Your port. The steps run from top to bottom. Your code sends SetRailVoltage(Ldo1, 2.8 V) to PF1550<Port>. A note over PF1550<Port> says: grid code, Limits window, rail declared. PF1550<Port> sends WriteRead(read LDO1_VOLT) to Your port. Your port returns true, byte to PF1550<Port>. A note over PF1550<Port> says: read-modify-write, IsWritable(). PF1550<Port> sends Write(LDO1_VOLT, new byte) to Your port. PF1550<Port> sends WriteRead(read LDO1_VOLT) to Your port. Your port returns true, byte to PF1550<Port>. A note over PF1550<Port> says: equal? else VerifyFailed. PF1550<Port> returns Result<void>{Ok} to Your code.
